clips.text: Cloudflare and Docker both show up in web projects.
Treating them as alternatives is like comparing a road network with a shipping box.
Docker packs an app with the pieces it needs: code, libraries, settings.
That package is an image. Run it, and it becomes a container.
Cloudflare does a different job: it sits in front of your site.
It can route visitors, keep copies of pages near them, and block bad traffic.
A team builds the app in Docker, runs it on a server, and puts Cloudflare in front.
Two layers, two jobs. The app is packed, the traffic is handled.
They are not competitors. Each does what the other does not. Cloudflare doesn't host your app. Docker doesn't secure it.
Docker packages the app. Cloudflare delivers and protects it. Different jobs. Sometimes, one stack.
